text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: high error rate and node flaps in inference-cluster-prod-2, auto-alerting at 10% request failure (Xid resets + OOM) — link: https://monitoring.redwood/prod/alerts/7892

Alex C: grabbing it. symptoms? which model pools?

Jen R: seeing recurring kernel Xid 31/43 in dmesg and occasional ECC messages. errors align with spikes around 10:12-10:18 UTC. pod restarts happening on node gpu-prod-2b.

Alex C: logs?

Jen R: paste of dmesg snippet:

```
[  630.412345] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 43, pid=20123, 0x00000007
[  630.412678] kernel: GPU ECC error detected on GPU 0, memory scrub triggered
[  630.412999] nvidia: GPU at 0000:65:00.0 has experienced a driver reset
```

Mike S: also seeing OOM killer messages inside the runtime container just before the driver reset. model batch sizes were peaking due to a traffic burst.

Alex C: immediate mitigation plan: 1) isolate affected node, 2) redirect traffic off node, 3) scale up spare capacity and promote fallback model variants, 4) attempt driver restart if safe, 5) escalate to infra if hardware ECC persists.

Tara P: I can take traffic cutover + customer comms. Alex, can you do node isolation and driver restart steps?

Alex C: on it. cordoning node now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-prod-2b
kubectl drain gpu-prod-2b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

Ops-Bot: nodes/gpu-prod-2b cordoned. Evicting pods.

Alex C: routing rules updated to avoid node: updating service router to prefer region-prod-1 and spare pool. Also setting temporary rate limit to reduce peak batch sizes for heavy customers.

Elaine C: customer impact — initial check: two customers had elevated 500s and slower streaming: acme-inc (tenant-acme) and beacon-health (tenant-beacon). I've opened CS tickets: CS-1029, CS-1030 and notified account owners. No SLA breaches yet but errors > threshold for some endpoints.

Jen R: attempted controlled driver restart on node (ssh -> sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service). nvidia-smi returns blank for a second then reports GPUs but dmesg still shows Xid 43 immediately after restart.

Infra-Team: if Xid persists after driver restart and ECC messages are present, flag as hardware-level. Recommend taking GPU out-of-service and initiating hardware replacement/workorder.

Alex C: pulled troubleshooting commands run:
```
ssh root@gpu-prod-2b
sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200
sudo dmesg | tail -n 60
nvidia-smi -q | egrep -i "xid|ecc|reset"
kubectl get pods -o wide --all-namespaces | grep gpu-prod-2b
```

Jen R: results pasted: several pods were OOM-killed (runtime: inference-engine) and one flink job had long GC pauses. Memory usage on GPU device shows ECC errors incrementing.

Mike S: temporarily scaled the dedicated pool by +2 instances and brought up quantized-fallback model (lower memory) for critical routes. Canary traffic routed to fallback at 5% then 20%.

Alex C: good. I'll leave node cordoned and marked unschedulable. Put a maintenance annotation and create a chassis ticket.

Ops-Bot: annotation applied: kubernetes.io/maintenance=cordoned-xid-1781123456

Tara P: handoff to next on-call (Tara P) in 30 min. summary for next oncall: node gpu-prod-2b cordoned/drained, driver restart attempted (Xid still observed), spare capacity provisioned, fallback model promoted, customers acme-inc/beacon notified. Follow-ups: open vendor support with Nvidia, run memtest on GPU, schedule hardware swap if ECC increases, post incident on status page if degradation persists.

Tara P: acknowledged. I'll take the handoff. next steps for me now: verify traffic stabilization, monitor Xid/ECC counters, confirm CS ticket updates, and coordinate replacement if infra says hardware.

Elaine C: prepping short customer note to be ready if we need to expand comms.

Alex C: filed infra ticket INFRA-8786 with logs and request for on-site diagnostics. tagging @Infra-Team.

Infra-Team: acknowledged, starting hardware runbook. ETA for hardware check is 6 hours due to parts schedule.

IncidentBot: Incident created INC-2026-1781123456, severity S2.

Mike S: quick workaround note — we set model routing policy to fallback for tenant-acme to keep their critical flows under lower memory footprint.

Tara P: leaving a runbook entry in incident tracker with commands executed and links to logs: https://internal.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-1781123456

Alex C: final note before handoff: do not uncordon gpu-prod-2b until infra clears it. If Xid frequency drops with node out of rotation we can close active incident but keep follow-ups.

Elaine C: will update CS tickets and ping account owners.

Jen R: monitoring shows 500->2% for the cluster now, latency back to baseline for most tenants. continuing to watch ECC counter.

Tara P: thanks team. I'm on for the next 4 hours. Please DM me if hardware vendor responds. :thumbsup:

Alex C: :thumbsup: great job everyone, will take a forced restart snapshot and attach to INFRA-8786.

Ops-Bot: deploy-bot reports no pending infra deploys.

IncidentBot: auto-log closed for active responders at 1781124100 (handoff complete).
